title: Diagonal preserves degreewise weak equivalences of bisimplicial sets
statement: A bisimplicial set is a functor $D:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]; its diagonal has $(\operatorname{diag}D)_n=D_{n,n}$, with both simplicial operators applied together. Use weak homotopy equivalences as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For any morphism $D\to E$ of bisimplicial sets, if $D_{m,\bullet}\to E_{m,\bullet}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $m$, then $\operatorname{diag}D\to\operatorname{diag}E$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The same holds with the two directions exchanged. In particular, if every structure map of the simplicial diagram $m\mapsto D_{m,\bullet}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, the map from the constant diagram on $D_{0,\bullet}$ induced by the unique maps $[m]\to[0]$ has diagonal a weak homotopy equivalence $D_{0,\bullet}\to\operatorname{diag}D$.
